name: Bharti Hexacom Ltd
title: Bharti Hexacom Ltd - 544162 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

capex.peers_comment: Airtel parent is stepping up data-centre and cloud capex; Hexacom says data centre is a separate entity and not applicable to telco.

summary.headline: Bharti Hexacom Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% QoQ to Rs2,510 Cr with EBITDAaL margin of 48.2%, while homes net adds slowed to 75k.
summary.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs2,510 Crores, up 4% sequentially, with EBITDAaL of about Rs1,210 Crores at a 48.2% margin. Mobile added about 210,000 net customers on a 29 million base, with ARPU at Rs259 helped by one extra day. Homes, office and other business net adds were 75k and revenue grew about 8% sequentially; management attributed the slower homes intake to a deliberate tightening of acquisition quality. Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) was about Rs830 Crores and net debt excluding leases was about Rs960 Crores (0.2x EBITDAaL). The call was a joint Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom webinar, and most Q&A addressed group-level topics.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex)
Homes, office and other net adds

segments.name: Mobile
segments.commentary: Added about 210,000 net customers and 344,000 smartphone customers; ARPU Rs259 with one extra day. Management flagged seasonality, expecting stronger customer additions in the second half of the year.

segments.name: Homes, office and other
segments.commentary: Net adds of 75k, with revenue up about 8% QoQ. IPTV rollout is adding depreciation; EBIT margin for the CPE-based homes business is negative or immaterial until scale is reached.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance given for Hexacom. Management expects homes acquisition quality to recover, with momentum seen in the last few weeks and some unwinding expected in the next one to two quarters.
Management said it cannot give a timeline for the homes EBIT margin turning positive, but says unit economics are the same as peers and it will turn positive at scale.
Capex priorities are 5G densification, network modernisation, fiberisation and homes/IPTV; management said it will spend adequately if needed for competitive growth.
Management said it would provide the count of the roughly 15-17 of the 400 relevant cities that fall in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, a figure it did not confirm on the call.
capex_capacity: Capex directed to 5G densification, network modernisation, and growing the homes and IPTV business; the quarter's capex figure was not disclosed separately.
Fiberisation remains a large ongoing task; Hexacom does not have the B2B/data-centre capex that sits in Bharti Airtel.
Depreciation rose 4.9% QoQ, driven by one extra day and rising IPTV rollout costs.
Hexacom operates in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, where it uses a mix of wireless and wired lines because of terrain.
demand_pricing: Mobile ARPU Rs259 with one extra day; the group-level pricing debate centred on the need to repair the tariff architecture to charge for data, with the group expecting ARPU growth of 4-5% over five to seven years.
Homes acquisition was tightened after the FWA push brought weaker quality and higher churn; management said fundamentals of the homes market have not changed.
Rajasthan was described as extremely competitive, while the Northeast position is comfortable; intensity on customer acquisition is said to be no different from other circles.
Management said refurbished phones are circulating more with smartphone inflation, but no impact on data sub-additions is seen so far.
International roaming is improving from the prior-quarter West Asia-related decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did mobile net adds weaken this quarter versus history, and was it circle-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray said there is normal seasonality in customer depletion across the industry over 16-20 quarters and that additions typically pick up in the second half of the year. He declined to call out a circle-specific cause.

qa_highlights.question: Has the homes outlook changed given acquisition-policy changes and rising chipset costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no change in the market size, share-gain or pricing assumptions. The slowdown reflects a one-quarter correction in acquisition quality, which management expects to unwind in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why are energy costs lower year on year despite higher diesel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Karthikeyan Velu cited seasonal solar-powered tower benefits and some one-offs. Soumen Ray added that diesel stock in DG sets means the full diesel price impact has not yet flowed through, and that the underlying sequential trend is as planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise 4.9% QoQ, and when will homes turn profitable at EBIT?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose because of one extra day and the IPTV rollout. Management gave no timeline for homes EBIT turning positive, but said it will once the business reaches scale, and that fiber rental versus owned fiber makes little difference at the EBIT level.

qa_highlights.question: How many of the 400 relevant cities are in Hexacom's circles, and how big is the homes opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray estimated about 15-17 of the 400 cities are in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, and said the figure would be confirmed later. Wireless plus wired is the chosen strategy in these terrain-heavy circles.

risks_watch: Homes net adds stayed weak this quarter because of tighter acquisition quality; the next one to two quarters need to show a recovery.
FWA economics face pressure from higher memory and chipset prices, and the FWA pivot to fiber could slow rollout in some areas.
Homes EBIT remains negative or immaterial, and no timeline has been given for it turning positive.
Diesel price impact has not fully flowed through; energy-cost tailwinds may reverse in coming quarters.
Smartphone inflation and refurbished phone circulation could affect the customer wallet over time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the underlying franchise and the quarter's numbers, but cautious and somewhat defensive on homes, where management described a deliberate, temporary slowdown in acquisition. Answers on Hexacom-specific margin and timing were brief and non-committal.
key_quotes: We ended the quarter with mobile customer base of 29 million with net customer additions for the quarter coming in at about 210,000.
Our operating free cash generation, which is EBITDAaL minus capex, came in at about Rs.830 Crores.
There is no fundamental change either in the assumption of how big is the market to how we need to gain share and three, how we need to price our offerings and give converged solutions.

adds.what: IPTV rollout for homes business (no capacity count or capex disclosed)

growth.why: No numerical revenue guidance was given; management expects homes acquisition quality to recover within one to two quarters and mobile net adds to be stronger in H2, but capacity additions and capex amounts were not quantified, so backing is vague.
